answer: Each applicant stores one meadow seed lot in a quartz capsule on a ledge shelf and locks a 70-credit bond. Its key-signed label states species and declared germination rate. An auditor samples it and runs a germination test; a rate over 5 points below declaration, a reused capsule, or a shared label burns the bond. The first shelf fee is 27; the kth is 27+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5022 and 1000 fakes pay 2,524,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-seed ring fails: its relabeled lot shares the seal and germination profile. An honest grower pays 27 once and recovers the bond after passing.
